observations: Under forced scroll every box is a steering instruction; sides alternate almost box by box, producing a slalom beat every 1-2 s.
Single boxes sit on the far bank of jumps and C3 sits on a landing: the box is the landing marker.
Ice removes steering; ice groups test lane commitment before the patch, first with boxes (S1-d) then with Nitros (S3-b).
All six TNT are pre-lit timed gates that count themselves; the speed burst becomes a risk (POINT 6).
Collectible density is flat (10/5/5/7 incl. C and 1UP) while explosive density rises (0/3/6/9).
Rewards sit on the exit line of hazards (S4-b after the Nitro zone, 1UP after C1).
Count traps are lateral, not hidden: S2-b contradicts the orca-safe line, S4-e zig-zags, S4-d is missing from F2, the green ! is off the bear.
Multi-box groups run along one lane (S2-c, S3-c/d, S4-b) so one held lane collects them at speed; only S1-a and S4-e spread across lanes.
Checkpoints split boxes evenly (10/18/29 of 45) and sit in calm beats.
A missed box cannot be recovered under forced scroll: the all-box goal is four perfect segments.
openQuestions: 3 boxes unlocated (48 PS1 vs 45 mapped = N. Sane 45): possibly boxes destroyed by pre-lit TNT before arrival, Nitros under the POINT 9 callout, or a version difference.
Five plain icons are wood? (could be striped).
S4-a Nitro positions approximate; 8 is a minimum.
